content: The base of the lung is broad and concave in shape. It rests upon the convex surface of the diaphragm, which serves as a partition between the thoracic and abdominal cavities. On the right side, the diaphragm separates the right lung from the right lobe of the liver. On the left side, it separates the left lung from the left lobe of the liver, the stomach, and the spleen. Due to the anatomical positioning of the diaphragm, which extends higher on the right side compared to the left, the concavity of the base of the right lung is deeper than that of the left lung. Laterally and posteriorly, the base of the lung is bordered by a thin, sharp margin. This margin projects into the phrenicocostal sinus of the pleura, which is the space located between the lower ribs and the costal attachment of the diaphragm. The base of the lung exhibits dynamic movement during respiration. It descends during inspiration as the lungs expand and ascends during expiration as the lungs recoil.
